mainTopic: Whether a קטן can father a child, the three-month בן סורר ומורה window, and whether we follow the majority in דיני נפשות
overview: The amud opens by finishing רבה's proof from the word ״אִישׁ״ that a קטן cannot father a child. אביי objects that a nine-year-old counts as a 'man' for relations, and רבה answers that his seed is like unripe grain that cannot grow. A teaching from דבי חזקיה backs רבה, and the פסוק about יעקב cooking a stew shows that מֵזִיד can mean heating. The גמרא then challenges רבה from the rule that a בן סורר ומורה must be a ״בֵּן״ and not a father, since the three-month window seems too short for a child to be both conceived and born in it. The answer is that a boy whose wife has conceived is already 'fit to be called a father.' Next the גמרא explains רבי כרוספדאי's three-month rule: the period ends at three months or when the beard surrounds, whichever comes first. רבי יעקב מנהר פקוד draws from this a lesson about seven-month pregnancies, and רבינא pushes it off by saying the rule follows the majority. That opens a debate over whether we follow the majority in דיני נפשות, and רבינא and רבי ירמיה מדפתי bring two משניות to show that we do. The explanation of the second משנה continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The word 'man' shows a minor convert has no relatives
steps.stepSummary: רבה finishes his proof. The תורה says ״אִישׁ״ in the law of stealing from a גר, so only for an adult גר do we need to check for relatives. A minor גר surely has none, because a קטן cannot father children.
steps.simpleTranslation: The תורה said ״אִישׁ״ ('man'). For a man, you need to check whether he has relatives or not. For a קטן, you don't need to check, because it is known that he has no relatives.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing רבה's proof that a קטן cannot father children. It uses the word ״אִישׁ״ in the פסוק about returning stolen money to a גר who has no relatives.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A גר has no family from before he converted, so his only possible relatives are children born after his conversion. The פסוק says ״אִישׁ״ to teach that only an adult גר needs to be checked for such children. A minor גר is assumed to have no children, which shows that a קטן cannot father a child.

keyTerms.meaning: The Merciful One, a name for ה׳ used when quoting the תורה
Relatives or heirs who would receive what is owed to the person
To go around checking about him
A minor, a boy under thirteen
It is known for certain

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the main claim of the whole section: a קטן cannot father children. Everything that follows either attacks or supports this.

phrases.english: And the Merciful One said: "man."
phrases.notes: במדבר 5:8: ״וְאִם אֵין לָאִישׁ גֹּאֵל״, the law of returning stolen money when the victim has no heirs.

phrases.english: A man – you need to go around checking about him

phrases.aramaic: אִם יֵשׁ לוֹ גּוֹאֲלִין וְאִם לָאו.
phrases.english: whether he has relatives or not.

phrases.aramaic: קָטָן – אִי אַתָּה צָרִיךְ לַחֲזוֹר עָלָיו,
phrases.english: A minor – you do not need to go around checking about him,
since it is known that he has no relatives.
phrases.notes: He means a minor גר could not have had children since converting, so there is no one to check for.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַחֲמָנָא: ״אִישׁ״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רבה's derivation begun earlier on the daf
steps.raayaSupportSource: The word ״אִישׁ״ in במדבר 5:8 regarding גזל הגר

steps.title: אביי objects: a nine-year-old is counted like a man
steps.stepSummary: אביי brings a ברייתא about relations with a שפחה חרופה. It includes a boy of nine years and one day under ״וְאִישׁ״, because he is fit for relations. This seems to show that a nine-year-old is treated like an adult man, against רבה.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי objected: 'Man' – this teaches only about a man. From where do we know about a boy nine years and one day old, who is fit for relations? The verse says 'And a man.'
steps.whatsHappening: אביי challenges רבה with a ברייתא. It treats a boy of nine years and a day as a full 'man' when it comes to relations.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא learns from the extra ו in ״וְאִישׁ״ that a nine-year-old's relations count fully, just like an adult's. אביי reads this as showing that a nine-year-old can also father a child. If so, רבה's claim that a קטן cannot father children seems wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: I only know about... (the plain meaning covers only this case)
Fit for marital relations
The פסוק teaches

phrases.english: Abaye raised an objection to him:
"Man" – I only know about a man.
phrases.notes: This is the פסוק about a שפחה חרופה, ויקרא 19:20.

phrases.english: A boy nine years and one day old
who is fit for relations, from where do we know?
The verse teaches: "And a man."
phrases.notes: The extra letter ו, meaning 'and,' adds the nine-year-old.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵיתִיבֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבה's claim from step 1
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה's claim that a קטן cannot father children
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא counts a nine-year-old as a 'man' for relations, which suggests he is like an adult and can father a child.

steps.title: רבה: he has seed, but it cannot produce a child
steps.stepSummary: רבה answers that a nine-year-old does have seed, so his relations count. But the seed cannot produce a child, like grain that was cut before it grew a third of the way.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: He has seed but cannot father a child. It is like grain that did not reach a third of its growth.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה answers אביי's objection. Being able to have relations is not the same as being able to father a child.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה splits the two things apart. A nine-year-old has seed, so his relations count, as the ברייתא says. But that seed is like unripe grain, which will not grow even if you plant it. So רבה's claim that a קטן cannot father children still stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Fathers a child
Grain
A third, here a third of the grain's full growth
Is similar to, is like

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up 'fit for relations' with 'able to father a child.' רבה agrees a nine-year-old has relations that count; he only denies that a child can come from them.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: יֵשׁ לוֹ וְאֵינוֹ מוֹלִיד,
phrases.english: He said to him: He has seed, but he cannot father a child,
it is like grain that did not reach a third of its growth.
phrases.notes: Grain cut that early won't sprout if you plant it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: יֵשׁ לוֹ וְאֵינוֹ מוֹלִיד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אביי's objection from step 2
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction: being able to have relations is separate from being able to father a child
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since a nine-year-old counts as a 'man' for relations, he can also father children
steps.terutzMaskana: A nine-year-old has seed, but it cannot produce a child, like unripe grain

steps.title: Support from דבי חזקיה: only a man produces viable seed
steps.stepSummary: A teaching from דבי חזקיה reads ״וְכִי יָזִד אִישׁ״ as a hint: an adult man can heat up and produce seed that works, but a קטן cannot. This supports רבה.
steps.simpleTranslation: דבי חזקיה taught: ״וְכִי יָזִד אִישׁ״ ('And if a man comes intentionally') – a man heats up and produces seed, but a קטן does not heat up and produce seed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא from the school of חזקיה that backs up רבה. It finds in a פסוק a hint that only an adult can produce seed that makes a child.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word יָזִד in the פסוק means 'acts on purpose.' The ברייתא also connects it to 'heating up.' Because it sits next to the word ״אִישׁ״, it teaches that only an adult heats up and produces seed that works, which is exactly רבה's point.

keyTerms.meaning: The study hall of חזקיה taught (a ברייתא)
Acts on purpose; here also read as 'heats up'
Heats up
Produces seed

steps.whatToRemember: רבה's view is backed by a ברייתא: a קטן may have relations, but cannot produce seed that fathers a child.

phrases.english: The school of Chizkiya taught:
"And if a man comes intentionally [yazid]" –
a man heats up and produces seed,
but a minor does not heat up and produce seed.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּבֵי חִזְקִיָּה תָּנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא supporting רבה's position after his answer to אביי
steps.raayaObject: A קטן cannot produce seed that fathers a child
steps.raayaSupportSource: ברייתא of דבי חזקיה on ״וְכִי יָזִד אִישׁ״ (שמות 21:14)

steps.title: רב מרדכי asks: how do we know מֵזִיד means heating?
steps.stepSummary: רב מרדכי asks רב אשי where we see that the word מֵזִיד has to do with cooking or heating.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב מרדכי said to רב אשי: From where do we know that this word מֵזִיד is a term for cooking?
steps.whatsHappening: רב מרדכי asks a question about a word. He wants to know the source for reading מֵזִיד as 'heating.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually מֵזִיד means 'on purpose,' so the ברייתא's reading needs a source. This is not an attack on the ברייתא; he only wants to know where this meaning of the word comes from.

keyTerms.meaning: From where can we tell? What shows that...?
A term, a way of speaking
Cooking

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב מָרְדֳּכַי לְרַב אָשֵׁי:
phrases.english: Rav Mordekhai said to Rav Ashi:
From where can we tell that this word "mezid"
is a term for cooking?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי מַשְׁמַע דְּהַאי ״מֵזִיד״ לִישָּׁנָא דְּבַשּׁוֹלֵי הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the word meaning used in step 4
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source showing that מֵזִיד can mean heating or cooking

steps.title: The source: יעקב cooked a stew
steps.stepSummary: The answer comes from the פסוק ״וַיָּזֶד יַעֲקֹב נָזִיד״, where the same root means cooking.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: ״וַיָּזֶד יַעֲקֹב נָזִיד״ ('And יעקב cooked a stew').
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers רב מרדכי's question with a פסוק. In it, the same root clearly means cooking.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the story of יעקב and עשו, ״וַיָּזֶד״ means 'cooked' and נָזִיד means 'stew.' Since the root ז-י-ד is used for cooking there, the ברייתא may read מֵזִיד as 'heating up.'

keyTerms.meaning: As it is written
And he cooked
A cooked stew

steps.whatToRemember: The root ז-י-ד can mean cooking or heating, as in ״וַיָּזֶד יַעֲקֹב נָזִיד״. This is how דבי חזקיה learns that only an adult 'heats up' and produces seed that works.

phrases.english: As it is written: "And Jacob cooked [vayyazed] a stew."

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּכְתִיב: ״וַיָּזֶד יַעֲקֹב נָזִיד״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב מרדכי's question from step 5
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק ״וַיָּזֶד יַעֲקֹב נָזִיד״ shows the root ז-י-ד means cooking

steps.title: A teaching that a son, not a father, can be a rebellious son
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings the teaching of דבי רבי ישמעאל that a בן סורר ומורה must be a ״בֵּן״ and not a father, as the start of a challenge against רבה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the school of רבי ישמעאל taught: 'A son' — and not a father.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new source to challenge רבה's view that a קטן cannot father a child. This line only sets up the challenge. The next step shows how it attacks רבה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says ״בֵּן סוֹרֵר וּמוֹרֶה״, and דבי רבי ישמעאל learn from the word ״בֵּן״ that someone who is already a father cannot become a בן סורר ומורה. The question this raises is how a boy that young could already be a father.

keyTerms.meaning: The stubborn and rebellious son of the Torah
The study hall (school) of רבי ישמעאל
But wasn't it taught? This phrase opens a challenge from a ברייתא

phrases.english: But didn't the school of Rabbi Yishmael teach:
'A son' — and not a father?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא תָּנָא דְּבֵי רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the proof for רבה from ״וְכִי יָזִד״, the גמרא brings a new source that seems to go against him.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה's view that a קטן cannot produce a child
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא assumes a boy in the בן סורר ומורה age range could already be a father. The next step will show this probably means a קטן fathered a child.

steps.title: The only way he could be a father is as a minor
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows that a boy can only be a father within the short בן סורר ומורה window if the child was conceived while he was still a קטן. So a קטן can father a child.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the case? Suppose the wife conceived after he grew two hairs and gave birth before the beard surrounded. Is there that much time? רבי כרוספדאי said the whole period of a בן סורר ומורה is only three months! So it must be that she conceived before he grew two hairs and gave birth before the beard surrounded. Learn from this: a קטן can father a child!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא works out the case behind the ברייתא. It concludes that the boy must have fathered the child while he was still a קטן, which goes against רבה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For the ברייתא's rule to matter, the boy must already be a father while still inside the בן סורר ומורה window. Pregnancy takes about nine months, but the window lasts only three months, from two hairs until the beard surrounds. So a child conceived after two hairs could not be born inside the window. The conception must have happened before he had two hairs, when he was still a קטן, and that proves a קטן can father a child.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the case? What are the circumstances?
Two hairs, the sign of physical maturity that makes a boy a גדול
The 'beard' (the lower hair) has grown all around, which marks the end of the בן סורר ומורה period
Enough time, an interval
Learn from this, a formula for drawing a conclusion

steps.confusionAlert: The 'beard' here is not a beard on the face. It means the lower hair growing all around, a later stage of maturity.

phrases.english: What are the circumstances?
If we say that she conceived
phrases.notes: He means the boy's wife became pregnant.

phrases.english: after he grew two hairs,
and gave birth before the beard surrounded —
is there such a long time?
But didn't Rabbi Kruspedai say:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל יָמָיו שֶׁל בֵּן סוֹרֵר וּמוֹרֶה
phrases.english: All the days of a stubborn and rebellious son
are only three months!
Rather, is it not that she conceived
before he grew two hairs,
and gave birth before the beard surrounded,
and learn from this: a minor can father a child!

steps.triggerLanguage: הֵיכִי דָמֵי? אִילֵּימָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: This step finishes the challenge that step 7 set up, by working out the only possible case.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה's claim that a קטן's seed cannot produce a child
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Nine months of pregnancy cannot fit into a three-month window. So the conception must have happened while he was a קטן.

steps.title: Maybe he became a father only after the window
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes off the proof. The wife really conceived after he grew two hairs, and the child was born after the beard surrounded.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. Really, she conceived after he grew two hairs, and gave birth after the beard surrounded.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the proof against רבה. The conception could have happened after the boy became a גדול.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the conception was after two hairs, the father was a גדול, so this is no proof that a קטן can father a child. The birth came after the window ended. That still leaves a question: how can the ברייתא's rule ״וְלֹא אָב״ matter at all? The next step answers it.

keyTerms.meaning: Really, actually. This word introduces the true way to read the case
A minor can father a child

phrases.english: No, really she conceived
after he grew two hairs,
and gave birth after the beard surrounded.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא, לְעוֹלָם דְּאִיעַבַּר בָּתַר דְּאַיְיתִי שְׁתֵּי שְׂעָרוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: This step rejects the conclusion of step 8 by reading the case differently.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof that a קטן can father a child
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Step 8 assumed the birth had to happen inside the window. The child could have been born after the window ended.

steps.title: Being fit to be called a father is enough
steps.stepSummary: רב דימי reports that in ארץ ישראל they read ״בֵּן״ as excluding anyone fit to be called a father. So a pregnant wife is already enough, even before the birth.
steps.simpleTranslation: And as for the difficulty from רבי כרוספדאי: when רב דימי came, he said that in the West they say, 'A son' — and not one who is fit to be called a father.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers how the ברייתא's rule can work inside a three-month window. Once his wife is pregnant, he is already 'fit to be called a father' and is exempt.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule ״וְלֹא אָב״ does not require the child to be born already. It is enough that he is on the way to being a father. So a conception after two hairs, within the three months, already exempts him, and we never have to say that a קטן can father a child.

keyTerms.meaning: In the West, meaning ארץ ישראל
One who is fit to be called a father, because his wife is already pregnant

steps.whatToRemember: The challenge against רבה falls away. ״בֵּן וְלֹא אָב״ excludes even a boy whose wife has only conceived, so there is no proof that a קטן can father a child.

phrases.english: And as for the difficulty from Rabbi Kruspedai —
when Rav Dimi came, he said:
they say in the West:
'A son' — and not one who is fit to be called a father.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּדְקָא קַשְׁיָא דְּרַבִּי כְּרוּסְפָּדַאי – כִּי אֲתָא רַב דִּימִי אֲמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: This step finishes the rejection in step 9 by solving the time problem that רבי כרוספדאי's rule raised.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reading the פסוק more broadly: 'father' includes one who is about to become a father
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A boy counts as 'a father' only once the child is born, so the conception must have come before the window.
steps.terutzMaskana: Once his wife conceives, he is 'fit to be called a father' and is exempt, so the conception can happen within the window after two hairs.

steps.title: The rule itself: the rebellious son period is only three months
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to examine רבי כרוספדאי's statement in the name of רבי שבתי that the whole בן סורר ומורה period lasts only three months.
steps.simpleTranslation: Returning to the statement itself: רבי כרוספדאי said in the name of רבי שבתי: all the days of a בן סורר ומורה are only three months.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now looks directly at רבי כרוספדאי's rule, which came up in the middle of the earlier discussion. This step sets up a question on it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule was only quoted in passing before. Now the גמרא brings its full source, רבי שבתי, so that it can test the rule against the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: The matter itself. The גמרא returns to examine a statement it quoted earlier
The source of the three-month rule

phrases.english: Returning to the matter itself: Rabbi Kruspedai said
that Rabbi Shabbtai said:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל יָמָיו שֶׁל בֵּן סוֹרֵר וּמוֹרֶה
phrases.english: All the days of a stubborn and rebellious son
are only three months.

steps.triggerLanguage: גּוּפָא, אָמַר רַבִּי כְּרוּסְפָּדַאי אָמַר רַבִּי שַׁבְּתַי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: This step goes back to a rule that was quoted in step 8 and examines it on its own.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The time in which a boy can become a בן סורר ומורה lasts only three months.

steps.title: But the משנה measures by body signs, not time
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי כרוספדאי from the משנה, which says the period runs from two hairs until the beard surrounds. That is a measure of the body, not of time.
steps.simpleTranslation: But we learned in the משנה: from when he grows two hairs until the beard surrounds!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how a fixed three-month limit can fit with the משנה, which sets the limit by signs of growth.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה ties the end of the period to a physical sign, the beard surrounding. If that sign comes late, the period could last longer than three months. So the two rules seem to clash.

keyTerms.meaning: But we learned in a משנה. This phrase opens a challenge from a משנה

phrases.english: But we learned in the mishna:
from when he grows two hairs
until the beard surrounds!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָאֲנַן תְּנַן: מִשֶּׁיָּבִיא שְׁתֵּי שְׂעָרוֹת וְעַד שֶׁיַּקִּיף זָקָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: This step attacks the rule that step 11 just stated.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה measures the period by a physical sign, not by time, so it could last longer than three months.

steps.title: Whichever comes first ends the period
steps.stepSummary: The period ends at whichever comes first: the beard surrounding, or three months passing.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the beard surrounded, he is exempt even if three months have not passed. If three months passed, he is exempt even if the beard has not surrounded.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that both limits are true. Whichever one comes first ends the בן סורר ומורה period.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה gives one end point and רבי כרוספדאי adds a second one. They do not clash, because each one can close the window on its own. So the period can never be longer than three months, and it can be shorter.

keyTerms.meaning: Even though
They were completed, here meaning the three months have fully passed

steps.whatToRemember: The בן סורר ומורה window starts at two hairs. It ends at whichever comes first: the beard surrounding or three months passing.

phrases.english: If the beard surrounded —

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל גַּב דְּלָא מְלוֹ שְׁלֹשָׁה חֳדָשִׁים.
phrases.english: even though three months have not passed, he is exempt.
If three months passed —
even though the beard has not surrounded, he is exempt.

steps.triggerLanguage: הִקִּיף זָקָן – אַף עַל גַּב דְּלָא מְלוֹ שְׁלֹשָׁה חֳדָשִׁים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: This step answers the challenge of step 12 by combining the two end points.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Both limits apply, and whichever comes first ends the period
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה's physical sign is the only end point, so the period could be longer than three months.
steps.terutzMaskana: The period ends either when the beard surrounds or when three months pass, whichever happens first.

steps.title: A lesson about seven-month pregnancies drawn from the three-month rule
steps.stepSummary: רבי יעקב מנהר פקוד, in the name of רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע, learns from רבי כרוספדאי's three-month rule that a woman who gives birth at seven months does not show her pregnancy after a third of her pregnancy.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יעקב from נהר פקוד sat before רבינא and said in the name of רב הונא son of רב יהושע: Learn from what רבי כרוספדאי said in the name of רבי שבתי that a woman who gives birth after seven months does not show her pregnancy after one third of her pregnancy.
steps.whatsHappening: A new אמורא uses the three-month rule from the last steps to learn something new about pregnancy. He states his conclusion here and explains how he got it in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a pregnancy becomes noticeable after a third of its length, which is three months in a nine-month pregnancy. רבי יעקב claims that a seven-month pregnancy is different. It does not become noticeable after a third of its length (two and a third months). It only shows at three months, like everyone else.

keyTerms.meaning: Learn from it: a conclusion drawn from an earlier statement
A woman who gives birth after seven months of pregnancy
Her fetus is noticeable, meaning the pregnancy can be seen
At one third of her days, meaning one third of the way through the pregnancy

phrases.english: Rabbi Yaakov from Nehar Pekod sat
before Ravina,
and he sat and said

phrases.aramaic: מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ:
phrases.english: in the name of Rav Huna son of Rav Yehoshua:
Learn from the statement of Rabbi Kruspedai
who said in the name of Rabbi Shabbtai,
a woman who gives birth at seven months:
her fetus is not noticeable at a third of her days.
phrases.notes: "Her days" means her pregnancy. A third of seven months is two and a third months.

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ מִדְּרַבִּי כְּרוּסְפָּדַאי אָמַר רַבִּי שַׁבְּתַי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the three-month limit settled in step 13 to draw a new conclusion about pregnancy.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A seven-month pregnancy is not noticeable after two and a third months. It becomes noticeable only at three months.

steps.title: Why the three-month limit proves this
steps.stepSummary: If a seven-month pregnancy showed after two and a third months, the בן סורר ומורה period would only need to be two and a third months, not three.
steps.simpleTranslation: For if you thought her pregnancy shows after a third of her pregnancy, why do I need three months? Two and a third months should be enough!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יעקב explains how he proved his point from the three-month rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The period ends once the boy could be called a father, and a noticeable pregnancy is already enough for that (step 10). If he had relations right when he grew two hairs, and she had a seven-month pregnancy that showed after two and a third months, his period would end then. Since רבי כרוספדאי gives a full three months, a seven-month pregnancy must not show before three months.

keyTerms.meaning: For if it would enter your mind: introduces an idea in order to reject it
Why do I need it?
Two and a third (months)
It is enough

phrases.english: For if it would enter your mind
that her fetus is noticeable at a third of her days,
why do I need three months?
phrases.notes: These are the three months of רבי כרוספדאי's rule from step 13.

phrases.english: Two and a third months should be enough!

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאִי סָלְקָא דַעְתָּךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reasoning behind the inference stated in step 14.
steps.raayaObject: A seven-month pregnancy is not noticeable after two and a third months.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי כרוספדאי's rule, in the name of רבי שבתי, that the בן סורר ומורה period lasts three months.

steps.title: רבינא: the rule follows most women
steps.stepSummary: רבינא answers that a seven-month pregnancy may really show after two and a third months. The three-month rule follows the majority of women, who give birth at nine months.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said to him: Really, I can tell you that her pregnancy does show after a third of her pregnancy. But go after the majority.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא pushes off רבי יעקב's proof. He shows that the three-month rule does not have to mean what רבי יעקב said.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Most women give birth after nine months, and their pregnancies show after three months. The rule was set by that majority, so the unusual seven-month case did not change it. The proof falls away, and a seven-month pregnancy could still show after two and a third months.

keyTerms.meaning: Really, I can tell you: keeps the original view while answering the proof
Go after the majority: follow what is true in most cases

phrases.english: He said to him:
Actually, I can tell you
that her fetus is noticeable at a third of her days.
Go after the majority.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְעוֹלָם אֵימָא לָךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in steps 14–15.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof. It leaves the three-month rule itself in place.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumes the rule must fit even rare seven-month pregnancies. In fact the rule is set by the majority, nine-month pregnancies.

steps.title: In capital cases we cannot just follow the majority
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע objects to רבינא. In דיני נפשות the תורה tells the court to try to save the accused, so it cannot ignore the minority case to execute him.
steps.simpleTranslation: They told this answer to רב הונא son of רב יהושע. He said: In דיני נפשות do we go after the majority? The תורה said, ״וְשָׁפְטוּ הָעֵדָה... וְהִצִּילוּ הָעֵדָה״ ('The congregation shall judge... and the congregation shall save'), and you say to go after the majority?!
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא's answer is brought to רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע, in whose name the original proof was said. He attacks the answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A בן סורר ומורה is put to death, so this is a case of דיני נפשות. The תורה requires the court to look for ways to save the accused. If a seven-month pregnancy could show after two and a third months, the boy might already count as a father then, so we should not punish him past that point. That would make the rule two and a third months, which brings back רבי יעקב's proof.

keyTerms.meaning: Capital cases, where a person's life is at stake
Do we go? A challenging question
The congregation shall judge and the congregation shall save: the court must look for ways to save the accused

steps.confusionAlert: רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע is not starting a new topic. He is defending the proof that was said in his own name in step 14, by knocking down רבינא's answer.
steps.whatToRemember: רבינא: the three-month rule follows most women. רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע: in capital cases the court cannot rely on the majority against the accused, because the תורה says ״וְהִצִּילוּ הָעֵדָה״.

phrases.english: They said it before
Rav Huna son of Rav Yehoshua.
He said to him:
But in capital cases
do we go after the majority?
The Torah said:
"And the congregation shall judge... and the congregation shall save,"
and you say, go after the majority?!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּבְדִינֵי נְפָשׁוֹת מִי אָזְלִינַן בָּתַר רוּבָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבינא's answer in step 16 and so brings back the proof of steps 14–15.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבינא's claim that the three-month rule simply follows the majority.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In capital cases the Torah requires the court to try to save the accused. It cannot set aside a real minority possibility that would free him just to follow the majority.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows a basic idea: in דיני נפשות the court leans toward saving the accused, even where it would normally follow the majority.

steps.title: רבינא answers: we do follow the majority in capital cases
steps.stepSummary: The objection is brought back to רבינא. He asks whether we really don't follow the majority in דיני נפשות, and he cites the משנה where one witness says 'the second of the month' and the other says 'the third', and their testimony still stands.
steps.simpleTranslation: They brought the objection back to רבינא. He said: Do we really not follow the majority in capital cases? But we learned in a משנה: if one witness says the event happened on the second of the month and the other says the third, their testimony stands. We assume one of them knew the previous month got an extra day and the other did not know.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא defends himself against the objection from Step 17. He points to a משנה that seems to follow the majority even in a capital case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 17 claimed that in דיני נפשות the court cannot rely on the majority. רבינא answers with a case where witnesses disagree on the date, and the court still accepts their testimony and can execute based on it. He will explain in the next step why this only makes sense if we follow the majority.

keyTerms.meaning: They brought it back before him
Capital cases, where a life is at stake
We follow the majority
Their testimony stands and is valid
Adding an extra day to a month, making it 30 days instead of 29

phrases.english: They brought it back before Ravina.
phrases.notes: "It" means רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע's objection from the last step.

phrases.english: He said to them:

phrases.aramaic: וּבְדִינֵי נְפָשׁוֹת לָא אָזְלִינַן בָּתַר רוּבָּא?
phrases.english: And in capital cases, do we not follow the majority?
But didn't we learn in a mishna:
One witness says "on the second of the month,"
and one says "on the third,"
their testimony stands,
because this one knows the month was extended by a day
and that one does not know.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּבְדִינֵי נְפָשׁוֹת לָא אָזְלִינַן בָּתַר רוּבָּא? וְהָתְנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: רבינא responds to the objection of Step 17 by questioning its basic premise.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim in Step 17 that the majority is not followed in דיני נפשות.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A משנה about capital testimony accepts witnesses who differ by a day, which suggests the majority is followed even when a life is at stake.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rejecting the premise of the objection
steps.terutzHavaAmina: In capital cases the court may not rely on the majority, so the three-month rule cannot be based on nine-month births.
steps.terutzMaskana: Even in capital cases we follow the majority, so רבינא's explanation still stands.

steps.title: Why the witnesses' testimony proves we follow the majority
steps.stepSummary: If we did not follow the majority, we would treat the witnesses as exact and say they contradict each other. Their testimony stands only because most people tend to make mistakes about the extra day of the month.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you think we do not follow the majority, then let us say these witnesses are speaking exactly and contradict each other. Rather, it must be because we follow the majority, and most people make mistakes about whether the month got an extra day.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא spells out exactly how the משנה proves his point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Without the majority rule, the court would have to consider that each witness meant his date exactly, which makes it a contradiction, and contradictory witnesses cannot convict. The משנה relies on the fact that most people get confused about the extra day, and that is following the majority. So even in a capital case, the majority is enough to accept testimony.

keyTerms.meaning: If it would enter your mind (if you were to think)
Go after the majority
Exactly, precisely
They contradict each other
They make mistakes

steps.whatToRemember: The two-witness date case shows that we follow the majority even in דיני נפשות, because the court relies on most people being unsure about the extra day of the month.

phrases.english: And if you were to think
that we do not say "follow the majority,"
then let us say: these witnesses are testifying exactly,
and they are contradicting each other!

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא לָאו מִשּׁוּם דְּאָמְרִינַן זִיל בָּתַר רוּבָּא,
phrases.english: Rather, isn't it because we say "follow the majority,"
and most people tend to make mistakes
about the extra day added to the month!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי סָלְקָא דַּעְתָּךְ לָא אָמְרִינַן זִיל בָּתַר רוּבָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how the משנה cited in Step 18 proves that the majority is followed in capital cases.
steps.raayaObject: That we follow the majority even in דיני נפשות.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה in סנהדרין where witnesses disagree by one day on the date and their testimony still stands.

steps.title: A second proof from the girl of three years and one day
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה מדפתי says another משנה also shows this. It lists the full legal results of relations with a girl of three years and one day: קידושין, יבום, אשת איש, טומאה, תרומה, being disqualified from כהונה, and the death penalty for עריות.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ירמיה מדפתי said: We also learned this in a משנה. A girl of three years and one day can be betrothed through relations. If her יבם has relations with her, he acquires her. A man who has relations with her when she is married is liable for אשת איש. She makes the man who has relations with her impure, so that the bedding under him becomes impure like the bedding above him. If she marries a כהן, she eats תרומה. If a man who is disqualified has relations with her, he disqualifies her from כהונה. If any of the עריות listed in the תורה has relations with her, they are executed because of her, and she is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ירמיה מדפתי brings a second משנה to support רבינא. On this amud the גמרא only quotes the משנה; the explanation of how it proves we follow the majority comes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה treats relations with a very young girl as full legal relations, even to the point of the death penalty for אשת איש and עריות. That is a capital consequence. The גמרא is preparing to show that this ruling also depends on following the majority.

keyTerms.meaning: We also learned it in a משנה, a supporting source
She can be betrothed through relations
The brother of a man who died childless, who may marry the widow
A married woman, and relations with her are a capital sin
The forbidden relationships listed in the Torah

steps.confusionAlert: Don't expect the proof to be stated here. This step only quotes the משנה; the argument for how it shows we follow the majority comes on the next amud.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yirmeya of Difti said:
We also learned this in a mishna:
A girl three years and one day old
can be betrothed through relations,
and if her brother-in-law has relations with her, he acquires her as his wife,
and a man is liable for relations with her as with a married woman.
And she makes impure the man who has relations with her,
so that the bedding beneath him becomes impure like the bedding above him.
If she married a priest, she may eat teruma.
If one of the men who are unfit had relations with her,
he disqualified her from the priesthood.

phrases.aramaic: וְאִם בָּא עָלֶיהָ אֶחָד מִכׇּל הָעֲרָיוֹת
phrases.english: And if any one of the forbidden relatives
listed in the Torah had relations with her,
they are executed because of her, and she is exempt.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַף אֲנַן נָמֵי תְּנֵינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second source supporting רבינא's claim from Steps 18-19 that the majority is followed in capital cases.
steps.raayaObject: That we follow the majority even in דיני נפשות.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה in נדה about a girl of three years and one day, where relations with her can lead to the death penalty.
